title: Business directories and professional networks
note: A verified company is not automatically a qualified lead. A contactable person is not automatically a buyer.
do_not_mix_rule: Directory research runs as its own pass. It updates an existing business record rather than creating a second one.
objective: A verifiable identity and legitimate business activity
A plausible fit for actual services
A relevant commercial opportunity or reason for further investigation
An appropriate, publicly available business contact channel
not_the_objective: Collecting as many company names or email addresses as possible.
sources: Public LinkedIn company pages and professional posts
Founder and owner profiles when publicly accessible
Publicly listed partner and vendor directories
Public project listings and professional service requests
access_rules: Use permitted access methods and respect platform terms, privacy requirements and rate limits.
Do not collect unnecessary personal information.
discovery_categories: CRM implementation and business automation providers
Customer support and business process service providers
Small and medium-sized businesses with identifiable integration needs
agency_rule: For agencies, investigate whether white-label implementation or overflow technical capacity is a plausible offer.
direct_business_rule: For direct businesses, investigate whether publicly documented services, workflows or stated requirements create a relevant automation opportunity.
industry_membership_rule: Industry membership alone is not evidence of demand.

rules: Match the role to the service being offered; the most senior person is not always the best contact.
Use only publicly documented professional roles and business contact channels.
Do not invent names, job titles, email addresses, phone numbers or reporting relationships.
If the decision-maker cannot be verified, record the company-level contact channel and mark the individual contact as unknown.
A contact's professional relationship to the business must be verified before it is recorded.

A.name: Explicit commercial signal
examples: A public request for an automation implementation partner
A company seeking an external developer for a relevant project
A founder requesting recommendations for a specific integration
An agency advertising a need for contractors or implementation capacity

B.name: Specific operational or technical evidence
examples: The business publicly documents a particular integration requirement
A company describes a relevant operational workflow and asks for solutions
An agency lists services that closely complement implementation capabilities and publicly invites technical partners

C.name: Verified business with plausible service fit
examples: An established agency provides CRM implementation services
An e-commerce business operates a public online store
C.caveat: Discovery signals, not proof of an unmet need.

D.name: Weak or unverifiable lead
examples: An incomplete profile with no reliable business identity
An inactive or unverified directory listing
A company with no clear fit for supported services
A contact whose role or association with the business cannot be established

tier_mapping.note: Do not promote a Level C or D prospect to high-intent status merely because it matches an industry category.

research_workflow: Discover the business through a relevant directory or professional network.
Verify the official business name and website.
Confirm its location and business category when available.
Review its publicly described services and target customers.
Search for relevant commercial or operational signals.
Identify an appropriate business decision-maker if possible.
Verify the person's professional relationship to the business.
Identify a legitimate public business contact channel.
Match the potential opportunity to one supported service.
Select the closest relevant portfolio project.
Check for existing records in ClientOutreach.
Score the prospect and recommend the next action.
insufficient_evidence_rule: When evidence is insufficient, return the candidate as unqualified or requiring further research.

portfolio_matching.rule: Use the most relevant verified project, explain why it is relevant, and never attach the same example to every lead.
portfolio_matching.claim_restriction: Do not claim measured ROI, revenue improvements or production outcomes unless supporting evidence exists.

commercial_signal.question: Is there a specific requirement or meaningful opportunity signal?

service_fit.question: Does the opportunity align with actual capabilities?

contactability.question: Is there an appropriate, verified route to contact?

commercial_suitability.question: Is a paid pilot, project or recurring engagement plausible?

scoring.gate: A score represents research priority, not conversion probability. A directory listing alone must not generate a high commercial-signal score.

missing_value_rule: Use unknown or null for unavailable data. Never fabricate missing details.

preconditions: Why this specific business is relevant
Which supported service is most appropriate
What evidence justifies contacting it now
Why the recipient is an appropriate contact
What small, practical first engagement could be proposed
outreach_rules.agency_offer: Consider a white-label implementation or overflow delivery proposal when the evidence supports it.
outreach_rules.direct_offer: Focus on a specific, evidence-backed workflow opportunity.
must_not: Claim a company needs automation merely because it operates in a suitable industry
Misrepresent the sender as a job applicant, existing partner or referred contact
Contact the same unresponsive prospect repeatedly
outreach_rules.channel_rule: Use concise, individualized outreach on appropriate business channels and respect opt-outs.

rules: Combine independent evidence without conflating it.
Update the existing record rather than creating a duplicate.
Keep individual contacts distinct from the business entity.

learning_rule: Use outcomes to improve the scoring model. Do not infer interest from a message being delivered or viewed.
operating_principle: Verify the organization. Identify the relevant role. Find a credible commercial signal. Match it to an actual service. Then decide whether to contact the prospect.
preference_rule: Prefer fewer, better-qualified opportunities over large lists of unverified companies and contacts.

quantity_policy.rule: No numeric limit. Return every qualified business and no unqualified ones.
